slot.brief: Count the number of relations / subsets possible from a set with n elements (total, symmetric, etc.).

stem: Let $A=\{p,q,p,r\}$ and $B=\{1,1,2\}$. How many relations from $A$ to $B$ contain exactly $3$ ordered pairs?

verdicts.working: Repeated elements do not change a set, so |A|=3 and |B|=2. There are 6 possible ordered pairs; choosing 3 gives \(\binom{6}{3}=20\).

working:
$|A|=3$, $|B|=2$ (repeated entries do not add elements).
$|A	imes B|=3\cdot2=6$.
A relation with exactly $3$ ordered pairs is a choice of $3$ from these $6$.
$ inom{6}{3}=20$.
